literal: Desire, anger, delusion - of these three, [when] name perishes, perishes disease.
translation: When even the names of these three—desire, anger, and delusion—are destroyed, the disease of suffering will also perish.
modern: காமம், சினம், மயக்கம் ஆகிய இந்த மூன்றின் பெயரும் கூட இல்லாமல் அழிந்தால், ஒருவருக்கு வரும் துன்பமும் அழியும்.
explanation: This couplet identifies three root causes of human suffering: desire, anger, and delusion. It states that true perception involves eradicating these flaws so completely that even their 'name' (நாமம்) ceases to exist within the mind. When these three are entirely destroyed, the 'disease' (நோய்) of suffering that they cause will also perish. The metaphor of disease emphasizes that suffering is an affliction which can only be cured by removing its underlying causes.
